name: Valley of the Kings
category: Ancient Necropolis / Royal Tomb Complex / UNESCO World Heritage Site

location.region: Upper Egypt, West Bank of the Nile opposite Luxor

historical_description: The Valley of the Kings is a desert valley in the Theban hills where, for roughly 500 years during the New Kingdom, Egyptian pharaohs and powerful nobles were buried in elaborately decorated rock-cut tombs rather than in pyramids, partly in an effort to deter tomb robbers. The valley contains 63 known numbered tombs and chambers (designated KV1 through KV63), ranging from small pits to the sprawling multi-chambered tomb of Ramesses II's sons (KV5). Its most famous tomb is that of the young pharaoh Tutankhamun (KV62), discovered virtually intact by Howard Carter in 1922, one of the most significant archaeological discoveries of the 20th century. The valley is divided into the East Valley, where most royal tombs are located and where tourists visit, and the smaller West Valley.

construction_details.period_of_use: circa 1539–1075 BCE (18th through 20th Dynasties, New Kingdom)
construction_details.tomb_construction: Tombs were cut directly into limestone bedrock, featuring long descending corridors, pillared halls, and burial chambers, decorated with painted reliefs and religious texts such as the Book of the Dead, the Amduat, and the Book of Gates
construction_details.number_of_tombs: 63 numbered tombs and chambers discovered to date (KV1–KV63)
construction_details.notable_tombs: Tutankhamun (KV62), Seti I (KV17, the longest and most elaborately decorated tomb in the valley), Ramesses VI (KV9), Tomb of the Sons of Ramesses II (KV5, the largest tomb in the valley)

opening_hours.daily_hours: 06:00–17:00 (approximate, may extend slightly in summer months)
opening_hours.notes: Some tombs are rotated in and out of public access periodically for conservation purposes

ticket_price.included_access: Standard general ticket includes entry to three tombs (excluding certain premium tombs)
ticket_price.additional_fee: A small tram fee (approx. 20 EGP) is charged to reach the tombs from the visitor center
ticket_price.notes: Certain premium tombs (Tutankhamun, Seti I, and others) require separate tickets beyond the general three-tomb entry. Prices are set by the Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities and subject to revision.

best_visiting_time.time_of_day: Early morning at opening, both for cooler temperatures in the exposed desert valley and to avoid crowds in the narrower tomb passages
best_visiting_time.season: October to April; summer heat in the shadeless valley can be extreme
best_visiting_time.note: Tomb interiors are not air-conditioned and can be hot and humid due to visitor traffic

interesting_facts: Tutankhamun's tomb (KV62) is famous largely because it was discovered nearly intact in 1922 by Howard Carter, unlike almost every other tomb in the valley, which had been looted in antiquity.
KV5, the tomb built for the sons of Ramesses II, is the largest tomb ever found in the valley, with over 120 identified chambers.
The tomb of Seti I (KV17) is the longest and one of the most beautifully decorated tombs in the valley, stretching over 137 meters into the hillside.
The valley was chosen partly because a nearby pyramid-shaped mountain, al-Qurn, naturally overlooks it, potentially serving a symbolic function similar to a pyramid.
Only a rotating selection of tombs is open to the public at any given time, both to manage visitor numbers and to allow humidity-sensitive wall paintings to recover.
Photography inside tombs was historically restricted or required paid permits; policies have varied over time, so visitors should check current rules on-site.
unesco_status: Part of UNESCO World Heritage Site 'Ancient Thebes with its Necropolis' (inscribed 1979)
accessibility_notes: Terrain is uneven desert ground; tomb interiors typically require descending ramps or steps into narrow corridors, making most tombs difficult or inaccessible for wheelchair users. A tram serves the walk from the parking area to the valley entrance.
nearest_airport: Luxor International Airport (LXR), approx. 20 km away
